question: Should OpenClaw add dynamic ack reaction selection, and should the durable contract be a configured emoji array, deterministic/random strategy, rule-based selector, or model-driven pre-ack hook?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the choice changes a shipped cross-channel config/API surface and ack reactions are emitted before normal reply generation, so automation cannot safely choose the user-facing semantics.

options.title: Approve a shared selector contract
options.body: Add a backward-compatible ackReaction/ackReactions or selector strategy that preserves existing string configs and is implemented consistently across supported channels.

options.title: Keep single-value ack reactions
options.body: Defer dynamic selection and keep variability to manual message reactions plus existing lifecycle status reactions.

options.title: Design a plugin/channel hook first
options.body: Extend a typed plugin/channel seam before growing core config if maintainers want extension-owned pre-ack selection behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve a shared selector contract
recommendation.body: Add a backward-compatible ackReaction/ackReactions or selector strategy that preserves existing string configs and is implemented consistently across supported channels.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history on the shared ack helper, config surface, and prior review of this issue.
